newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money ends easy, gilts continue uptrend.
newsitem.headline: India call money ends easy, gilts continue uptrend.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday unchanged at 0.10-0.50 percent in a banking system awash with liquidity and dealers said rates were unlikley to move up from the current levels in the near future.
"Interest rates look like being stuck below 1.0 percent till at least mid-May," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "There is far too much liquidity in the system at the moment."
He said rates were unlikely to go up unless the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) mopped up funds at high rates through its repo auctions or government bond issues hit the market.

Dealers said prices of government securities continued rising on Tuesday. Prices have been on the rise through last month, driven by low call money rates and on market expecatations of a fall in interest rates.

The RBI unveiled its credit policy for the first half of 1997/98 (April-March) earlier on Tuesday, announcing a cut in the cap on deposit interest, among other steps intended to lead to a reduction in interest rates.
One state-run bank has already announced a 50 basis point cut in its prime lending rate to 14 percent per annum.

Dealers said the zero-coupon bond 2000 was traded on Tuesday at 69.30 rupees against its last traded price of 68.75 rupees, 13.62 percent 1998 at 105.82 against 105.25, 13.80 percent 2002 at 106.08 rupees against 105.70 and 13.50 percent 1997 102.70 rupees against 102.47.
